findings.title: Login cache invalidation can be skipped when the original IDP is org-disabled
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate evaluates getLoginPredicate() against the original model returned by getById(), which is wrapped by createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(). That wrapper's isEnabled() returns false whenever the associated organization (or the organization provider) is disabled, even though the raw IDP is enabled and may already be present in the login cache populated from the delegate. If an admin then updates that IDP while the organization is disabled, e.g. sets hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true, or enabled=false, the updated raw model also fails the predicate because of the changed login field. The method therefore returns at this guard without invalidating any cacheKeyForLogin entry, leaving the stale internal id in the login cache. After the organization is re-enabled, getForLogin() returns that IDP even though it is hidden/link-only/disabled; the new OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), so hidden or link-only IDPs can still be displayed. Cache membership must be compared using the same raw IDP state used to populate the delegate query, not the organization-aware wrapper.

findings.title: Cleanup removes literal alias 'alias' instead of the created alias
findings.body: The cleanup action is bound to testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, so the receiver is resolved immediately for an IDP whose alias is literally 'alias'. The IDPs just created as idp-alias-N are never removed, and the cleanup may also fail with a 404. The same mistake appears at line 425. This leaks up to 20 IDPs into the test realm and can make count-based assertions in this test class order-dependent. Use get(alias)::remove for the actual alias, or remove the created IDPs in @After.

findings.title: Positive create/remove invalidation paths for login IDPs are not tested
findings.body: The new test only creates and removes IDPs that do not qualify for login (disabled or hideOnLogin=true) and asserts that the login caches remain. The new registerIDPLoginInvalidation calls in create() and remove() are never exercised for a login-qualified IDP, so a regression where creating or removing a visible enabled IDP fails to invalidate the login caches would still pass this test. Add steps that populate the caches, then create and remove an enabled, visible IDP and assert all login caches are invalidated.
